title: Role-Playing Simulation Games using ChatGPT
extended_summary:
This paper explores how large language models, specifically ChatGPT, can be used to enrich teaching through role-playing simulation games. The authors frame the work as a way to move beyond passive lecture-based instruction and toward active learning, especially in digitally oriented higher education contexts.

The intervention described is a ChatGPT-enabled negotiation role-play in which students interact asynchronously with the chatbot as an interlocutor. A fixed prompt initiates the scenario, and students take on the role of advocating for and negotiating approval of a cloud migration project budget. The activity was implemented as a case study in the master's course "Impact of Cloud Computing on Organisations" within the "Cloud Computing Engineering" programme at the University of Applied Sciences Burgenland.

The paper argues that ChatGPT can be programmed to support realistic conversational simulations and that this can help students practice communication, negotiation, and decision-making skills in a flexible format that is not constrained by time or location. The authors present the work as an initial exploration rather than a conclusive evaluation, and they suggest future work involving additional prompts, scenarios, and master’s programmes to assess broader applicability.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a brief practice-oriented case description in an ERCIM News article, not a controlled empirical study. It reports no analytic methodology, comparison group, or quantitative outcomes, so it does not meet evidence standards for causal inference.
impact_tier_rationale: The article proposes a potentially useful classroom application of ChatGPT, but provides no measured effect sizes or robust outcome evidence. Impact is therefore unclear and modest at best, based on qualitative claims only.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used as a conversational role-play partner in an asynchronous simulation game for students to practice negotiation and decision-making in a cloud migration project scenario.
Role-playing simulation game design using ChatGPT to simulate real-life organizational negotiations and support active learning through practice.

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that using ChatGPT in a role-playing simulation can support durable skills such as negotiation, decision-making, critical thinking, and problem solving, but it reports no quantitative effect estimate. The evidence is a single illustrative case study in a master’s course (n not reported), so the finding is qualitative and preliminary rather than causal.
finding.measure: Qualitative course case study of student role-play performance and reflective experiences; no standardized outcome measure reported

finding.finding_summary: The article suggests the ChatGPT-based simulation may increase student interest and motivation by allowing learners to practice realistic scenarios independently. However, it provides no pre-post data, comparison group, or effect size, so the claim remains descriptive and speculative.
finding.measure: Observed student engagement/interest during the simulation; no formal scale reported
